scope: Lineage-mapped held-out DROID wrist-to-exterior calibrated depth-splat lower bounds
summary: Four episode/view lower-bound runs complete with verified raw alignment and camera chains, but sparse visible coverage and mixed PSNR reject depth splatting as a held-out novel-view solution.
evidence: Episode 21 wrist-to-exterior_1 reaches 3.586% mean coverage and 7.500 dB visible PSNR.
Episode 21 wrist-to-exterior_2 reaches 6.365% mean coverage and 16.439 dB visible PSNR.
Episode 77 wrist-to-exterior_1 reaches 14.222% mean coverage and 14.547 dB visible PSNR.
Episode 77 wrist-to-exterior_2 reaches 19.129% mean coverage and 9.145 dB visible PSNR.

All four runs use strict-free physical GPU 6, hash-bind the accepted raw-to-LeRobot alignment, preserve the swapped episode-local exterior assignment, and save source/target/warp/mask/depth artifacts for three sampled frames.
Cross-camera nearest-HDF timestamp offsets span -75 to +74 ms at the sampled frames.
lessons: Calibrated source-visible depth cannot fill target disocclusions and is only a geometric lower bound.
Correct camera lineage does not imply sufficient novel-view image quality.
The verified depth warp is useful as conditioning or a visibility mask, not as the final generator.
limitations: Only three depth samples per episode/view are evaluated.
Coverage is sparse and no disoccluded content is synthesized.
Raw DROID rights and episode-60 availability remain unresolved.
next_actions: Use the warp/mask/depth artifacts as explicit geometry conditioning for a learned real-data novel-view method.
Do not promote raw depth splatting as a novel-view baseline or SOTA result.
